learning_objective: 🎯 Uncover the immense forces and energy locked inside the atomic nucleus, explore radioactivity, and understand nuclear power!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: The nucleus is made of protons and neutrons (together called nucleons). Isotopes are atoms of the same element (same protons) but with a different number of neutrons (different mass).

If you weigh a nucleus, it is actually *lighter* than the sum of its individual protons and neutrons! The missing mass (Mass Defect) is converted into the Binding Energy that holds the nucleus tightly together, following Einstein's $E = mc^2$.

Unstable nuclei naturally break down over time to become stable, spitting out radiation. They emit Alpha particles (Helium nuclei), Beta particles (fast electrons), or Gamma rays (high-energy photons).
Radioactivity is random but predictable on a large scale. The 'Half-Life' ($T_{1/2}$) is the time required for exactly half of the radioactive nuclei in a sample to decay.

Fission: A heavy, unstable nucleus (like Uranium) is split into two lighter ones, releasing massive energy (used in nuclear power plants). Fusion: Two light nuclei (like Hydrogen) smash together to form a heavier one, releasing even MORE energy (powers the Sun!).

fun_activity.title: 🦖 Carbon Dating Concept
fun_activity.instructions: Did you know archaeologists use Carbon-14 (a radioactive isotope) to find the age of dinosaur bones? Since the half-life of Carbon-14 is 5,730 years, they just measure how much of it is left in the bone to calculate exactly when the animal died!

exam_tips: 📌 Study the Binding Energy per Nucleon curve carefully. Iron (Fe-56) is at the peak, making it the most stable nucleus in the universe.
📌 Understand that both Fission (heavy nuclei splitting) and Fusion (light nuclei joining) move atoms closer to the stable Iron peak, which is why both processes release energy.
📌 In radioactive decay equations, the total atomic number ($Z$) and mass number ($A$) must be balanced on both sides.
quick_recap: ⭐ The Strong Nuclear Force holding protons together is the strongest force in nature, but it only works at incredibly tiny distances.
⭐ $E=mc^2$ proves that mass and energy are just two forms of the exact same thing.
⭐ Stars shine due to continuous nuclear fusion reactions in their cores.
